summary: Prototype Rules enforce shared meal reads, owner/admin edits, multi-dish name claims, incrementally verified payment groups, immutable bank receipts and settlement markers, preserved money on paid edits/cancellations, and paired immutable administrator reconciliation events. Restaurant links allow only active, unexpired capability gets; administrative roles and private profiles remain restricted. Carryover adds same-owner source/target money transfers with immutable ledgers and controlled credit pointers. Activity history is administrator-readable and append-only; client events are identity-bound, bank acceptance events are paired with receipts.
verification: 59 tests passed against Standard Auth/Firestore emulators, including prior ordering/payment/role/share flows plus credit across days, exact cash shortfalls, simultaneous allocations, refund-choice races, forged paired transfers, guest-to-Google credit ownership, reversal after outgoing credit, and administrator-only immutable activity history. Build and type checking passed. Browser QA verified an 80k paid sample reduced to 40k, keeping 40k credit, applying it to a 50k meal and settling only the remaining 10k through a local fake bank notification. No production financial transaction was performed.

findings.issue: Anonymous sign-in and per-document bounds do not impose a trusted global write/request-rate limit.
findings.recommendation: Monitor usage; assess App Check and trusted rate limiting before broad public adoption.

findings.issue: Administrators are trusted to create restaurant JSON payloads. App projection omits user/payment fields, but free-text notes may contain personal information. Anyone holding an active link can access it, and downloaded copies cannot be revoked.
findings.recommendation: Review notes before sharing; revoke links when no longer needed. Use separate projects for untrusted previews.

findings.issue: App-origin events are client-reported. Direct external SDK/Console changes can bypass application telemetry, and visits may be absent while offline. Users can append claims about their own app activity; they cannot impersonate another actor or bank acceptance.
findings.recommendation: Use immutable receipts and paired financial/credit ledgers as the authority for money. Do not treat client telemetry as a forensic security audit. Add trusted database change capture separately if required.

findings.issue: Credit balances are derived from current source orders, and source pointers retain history. Read volume grows with the number of carryover sources.
findings.recommendation: Monitor Firestore usage and consider a trusted materialized balance/active-source index at larger scale without weakening paired-transfer validation.

assumptions: The existing primary admin UID PRIMARY_ADMIN_UID_HERE is bootstrapped in Console; only that enabled verified Google identity may change other administrator memberships in the web app. No self/primary role changes or blocks.
The client normalizes names to NFC and hashes lowercase text; Rules explicitly normalize Vietnamese uppercase Đ for matching browser-generated IDs.

The user explicitly requested shared visibility of all meal information. Rules apply to complete order documents, including notes, owner IDs and payment state; all Firebase visitors, including anonymous customers, can read these. Role documents and ownership-transfer tickets keep their existing private access checks.
Existing mealDays/mealOrders and old signed-cookie guest identities require a separate reviewed migration; this change does not import or expose them.

Pickup results are administrator-created assignments. Rules validate authority, date, roster closure, bounded values and immutability; the trusted admin application computes weekly priority and random tie breaks. History counts selections from feature activation, matched by normalized order name.

User-profile emails/provider are attested by Firebase identity token, readable by owner/admin only. The human explicitly requested a user-management directory for administrators; meal shared-read permissions do not expose these new private profile collections.

Ordering blocks apply to a UID, not Firebase Authentication deletion/disable. Anonymous identities can change after clearing browser data. Historical order owners appear without invented emails; live profiles are registered on later visits.

The deployment tolerates old Rules for optional self-profile sync/own-access reads until manual publication. Required directory and role/block operations still fail closed with a publication message. Browser name storage remains independent of Firebase profile readiness.

Raw BIDV notification delivery is trusted only through the configured Shortcut bearer; it is not a bank-signed webhook. A stolen bearer can forge text. No fuzzy name/date matching, partial amounts or automatic refunds. Unknown bank formats require a new tested parser.

Payment identity is an anonymous Firebase account with a server-only refresh token and primary-admin-granted enabled integration document, never an administrator. Integration revocation is checked by Rules on each read/write. Production ignores emulator endpoints. Account deletion/token revocation/anonymous auto-cleanup requires operational rotation.

Intents expire within 24h (client requests 23h), match immutable order creation and current meal/quantity/payee settings, and link to a current reference. Server reads are followed by an atomic conditional commit; Rules revalidate fresh bank/link/order state with paired records. Notification timestamps permit 2 minute rounding and 5 minute future skew.

Receipts retain only transaction/account/amount/time, integration UID and notification hash, not raw notification or ending balance. Unmatched notifications are returned to the Shortcut without altering orders. Financial confirmation from actual bank statements remains available for manual reconciliation.
